PullRequest.Title: canvases: replace VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR with Copilot home storage
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Canvas extensions created by `/create-canvas` live in `.github/extensions/`, so anyone working in the repository can load them in any Copilot host. But the skill told them to keep private data in `VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR`, which only VS Code's Agent Host sets. In the Copilot CLI and the GitHub app, those canvases can't save anything. In VS Code, plugin canvases lost their data on every plugin update, because the folder name was a hash of the extension's module path, which changes with each update.

## Changes

- **`/create-canvas` skill:** extensions build only on the Copilot SDK contract.
  - Private data goes in `<COPILOT_HOME>/extension-data/<canvas-id>/`. The Copilot home is `COPILOT_HOME`, or `~/.copilot` when unset; every Copilot host uses it, and extension processes inherit it.
  - The canvas ID names that folder, so it must be distinctive.
  - Records are keyed by domain identity, written atomically (temporary file, then rename), and validated on read.
  - VS Code-specific wording about the page bridge, closing tabs, and reopening is replaced.
- **Agent Host:** no longer sets `VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR` for extension processes. The launch test now checks the extension's entire environment.
- **Docs and spec:** `AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md` documents the new location. The skill spec requires the new storage rules and rejects any mention of VS Code.

## Breaking change

There's no deprecation period and no data migration. Existing data under `agentHostCanvasData/` stays on disk but is no longer read. Canvases that still read `VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR`, such as Agent Plan and kusto-canvas, can't save in VS Code until they move to the new location.

## How to test

Run on this branch after rebasing onto `main`:

- `cd extensions/copilot && npx vitest --run --pool=forks src/platform/promptFiles/test/node/builtinSkills.spec.ts`: passed (3 tests)
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` then `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --grep "launch"`: passed (11 tests)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts extensions/copilot/src/platform/promptFiles/test/node/builtinSkills.spec.ts`: passed
- `npm run precommit` (hygiene on the staged files): passed

Manual checks:

- I built a throwaway canvas by following an earlier draft of the skill. It reloaded, opened, ran an action, and kept its state when reopened, with data under `~/.copilot/extension-data/`.
- In a standalone script, six processes wrote the same file while another read it. Temporary-file-plus-rename writes gave 0 failed reads out of 41,269; plain `writeFile` gave 199 out of 41,700.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host creates or resumes a canvas-enabled Copilot session and launches discovered extension providers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Client startup resolves bundled runtime assets, then session initialization waits for extension readiness before the relevant model turn. For each provider generation, the SDK asks the unchanged launch provider for a command and launches the extension subprocess. The changed resolver only stops computing a SHA-1 and stops adding VSCODE_CANVAS_DATA_DIR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize a project extension module path with fs.realpath before launch admission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One realpath for each project-source launch resolution; user and plugin sources do not perform it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-project realpath ran before the diff, followed by an in-process SHA-1 and path join.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For project extensions it must complete before the launch command is returned and the provider can become ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the extension bootstrap process for each admitted extension provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess per provider generation as scheduled by the Copilot runtime; reload may start another generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same executable and bootstrap arguments launched the same subprocess; only one environment entry has been removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider readiness is awaited, with existing bounded readiness handling, before the relevant model turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered extension providers per create/resume/reload generation; project providers additionally incur one canonicalization each.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider process scheduling is owned by the Copilot runtime and is unchanged by this diff. Admission tracks approved roots per live session; there is no newly introduced burst or serialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Bundled runtime/bootstrap assets are resolved once per client residency. Warm sessions reuse the client; provider reload starts a new provider generation as before. The diff does not change cache keys, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete runtime hunk, caller, session initialization, launch tests, and canvas lifecycle integration test show unchanged boundary cardinality and a reduction in per-resolution CPU work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact provider counts and runtime scheduling vary by user configuration, but that does not affect the before/after conclusion because no boundary or concurrency increase is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes SHA-1 computation and one environment value from each resolution without adding filesystem, IPC, network, or subprocess work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A canvas generated from /create-canvas opens, reads private durable state, and writes state from actions across hosts or workspaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The skill now directs generated extensions to resolve COPILOT_HOME, create their data directory on first use, validate a selected record when opening/reading, and perform temp-file-plus-rename writes. Those filesystem operations are on the generated canvas open/action critical path only when that canvas actually requires private durable state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and validate a domain-keyed durable record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the record selected by the generated canvas operation; exact calls depend on generated extension logic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old skill specified a host-provided storage root but did not prescribe format/version/shape validation. The underlying durable-state read was still required by any stateful implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A generated open/action needing durable state waits for its selected read and validation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write a uniquely named temporary file and rename it over the target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two filesystem mutations per durable record write, independent of the total records stored.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old skill required durable storage but did not require atomic temp-file-plus-rename writes, so implementations could use one direct write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A generated state-changing action waits for the atomic write if its implementation persists synchronously with the action result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Durable-state reads and writes, keyed by the selected domain identity. Effective cardinality is one selected record per open/action rather than all repositories or all records; concurrent sessions may target the same record.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple hosts may call generated extension actions concurrently. Unique temporary files plus atomic rename avoid partial reads; the skill does not introduce a loop, Promise.all fan-out, queue, or shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold first use creates the extension directory; warm use reuses it. The guidance intentionally validates each read rather than caching potentially stale cross-process state. No in-memory cache, negative cache, or retained collection is introduced by the repository code itself.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the prompt now prescribes bounded validation and atomic filesystem work; low that any fixed workload or file size follows because generated implementations and requested canvas behavior determine both.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: State size, action frequency, and whether durable private state is needed are request-dependent. The added rename and validation are bounded per selected record and are justified by cross-process durability; no realistic scaling regression is established by this diff alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added I/O is bounded per durable write/read and preserves atomicity across hosts; the diff does not prescribe collection-wide scans, unbounded buffering, or per-item boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Built-in skill contract tests and Agent Host launch tests execute during development or CI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tests synchronously read the skill file and compare required anchors, or instantiate a test client and resolve launch metadata. They are not on an end-user startup, render, input, or session critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read SKILL.md synchronously in the built-in skill test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed file read per selected test execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same synchronous file read already occurred; only expected text changed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed skill file and a fixed number of launch-resolution assertions per test run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Test runner concurrency is unchanged; the modified assertions add no production concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Filesystem caching is controlled by the OS/test runner and unchanged. There is no new application cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed test hunks are fixed-size assertions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CI scheduling varies but the work is constant and materially unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No production performance impact and no meaningful CI scaling regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced session create/resume/reload, provider launch, generated canvas storage, and tests. The runtime change removes per-launch CPU work without increasing expensive-boundary cardinality; the prompt's new durability operations are bounded per selected record and do not establish actionable fan-out, retention, concurrency, or critical-path regression. No findings submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
